# normalizer　`def.normalizer`

## Notes · **draft**
⭐ Normalizer vs centralizer: $C_G(H) \subseteq N_G(H)$, and in general they are not equal. $N_G(H)/C_G(H)$ embeds into $\operatorname{Aut}(H)$ (by conjugation); this is the standard "normalizer modulo centralizer" statement.

⭐ Examples: in $S_3$, $N_{S_3}(\langle(12)\rangle) = \langle(12)\rangle$ (the three transpositions are conjugate to one another, so the normalizer does not grow); $N_{S_3}(A_3) = S_3$.

⚠ $N_G(S)$ only requires that the set $S$ be sent to itself, not that each element be fixed; the latter is the centralizer.

> Proofs of the edges are still Chinese only: `proofs/`; the Chinese page remains authoritative.
